title: Kantyna Nova tasting menu: neutralize nine mixed-light restaurant captures to an in-frame grey card, route each shot to its own treatment, build one authored house grade, and data-merge a press-ready one-dish-per-page menu

source.reference: Professional Photo Editor for Restaurant Brand

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Freelancer.com brief ('Professional Photo Editor for Restaurant Brand': 'improve the quality of photos for a new website for our restaurant and catering brand', 'improving overall image quality, sharpness, colors, lighting, and contrast', 'consistent color grading across all materials', 'creating a cohesive visual style for the entire website', 'retouching imperfections while maintaining a natural look'). The real client is a Polish catering brand; it is laundered to the FICTIONAL brand 'Kantyna Nova' with a fictional owner persona (Marta Zawadzka) — no real company, person, product or trademark is named anywhere. REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to fix the audited G6 defect (the prior version asserted cohesion with no measurable target, hand-graded ONE hero, then applied a STOCK built-in preset to seven siblings — a stock preset cannot reproduce a hand-built grade, so the set could never actually match and the grader had nothing to fail). The rebuild makes cohesion a real, checkable target: the client's photographer laid a photographic 18% grey card into the corner of every raw capture, so 'consistent visual style' becomes 'every card neutralized to one shared white point'. The agent builds ONE authored house look from primitive tone controls (there is no loadable preset) and holds it identical across the batch; each frame is neutralized to its OWN in-frame card by eye and the applied parameters are reported. The 'retouch imperfections / make the food read' ask is honored the connector-legal way — a subject-aware background depth-of-field blur on cluttered hero plates only (never inpainting/object-removal, never a whole-frame blur), routed per shot. The endpoint the brief actually rewards (a cohesive, premium set for the launch) is delivered as an agent-owned designed artifact: a press-ready tasting-menu PDF built by a genuine one-record-per-page InDesign data-merge, plus a monochrome ambience cover the agent authors. No generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no from-scratch art, no upscaling, no object-removal.
one_line_ask: Take nine raw Kantyna Nova restaurant captures shot under different lightings — each carrying an 18% grey card in frame — neutralize every one to the card so the whole set shares one white point, build and hold one authored premium house look across the batch, decide per shot which get a background separation and which must be left alone, then compose the graded dishes into a press-ready one-dish-per-page tasting menu and an authored monochrome ambience cover.
full_brief: Kantyna Nova is a modern Polish comfort-food restaurant and catering brand launching a new site and a printed tasting menu, and our food photography has to stop looking like nine unrelated snapshots and start reading as one deliberately-styled brand. We are NOT reshooting. We are handing you nine raw captures straight off a shoot day, and here is the real problem: they were shot in whatever corner of the room was free, so side by side they clash — some came out warm and orange under the tungsten pendants, some cold and blue by the north window, one has a sickly green cast from the old kitchen-pass fluorescents, one is a muddy underexposed mess, one plate is genuinely deep golden-brown and was shot under clean light so it already looks right, and a couple are tilted. Because we knew the light was a mess, our photographer clipped a neutral 18% grey card into the corner of every frame. That card is your ground truth. Job one, cohesion: make the whole set read as ONE set by neutralizing each frame to the grey card it carries — on every graded frame the card must read a clean neutral (no residual warm, blue or green tint) and land on the same mid-grey brightness as the rest, so once every card is neutral the batch shares one white point. Do NOT reach for a single blanket correction, do NOT copy one frame's numbers onto the others, and do NOT auto-tone each frame on its own: each frame was lit differently and a move that rescues one drives another further off, and an auto pass keys off each frame's own histogram so the casts will never agree and the set will visibly fail to match at the cards. Diagnosing what is actually wrong with each frame and choosing the control that clears it is your call, not ours. Be careful with the one plate that is genuinely golden and was shot clean — if its card already reads neutral, do not 'cool' it chasing a cast that is not there, or you will strip the real color of the food. When you are done, tell us the white-balance and exposure move you settled on for each frame so we can confirm they were matched to the cards, not eyeballed. The house look itself — a warm, rich, premium restaurant tone with lifted shadows, gentle contrast, the crispness that makes crumb and glaze and steam read, and a restrained pop so the food looks appetizing without going garish or plastic — is yours to build and hold identical across all nine; there is no preset to load, only our one-page look note. Job two, make the food the hero, but use judgement: several plates were shot on cluttered tables and the busy background fights the dish, so the dish needs to be lifted off its surroundings — but some plates were already shot clean, and two of these captures are overhead spreads where the whole surface IS the subject and there is no single hero to isolate. Treat each shot as it needs and leave the ones that are already working alone; getting that wrong quietly ruins a shot and nobody notices until it prints. Keep everything natural — no over-processing. Deliverables: (1) the nine graded masters as a contact set our marketing lead can eyeball against the cards; (2) a press-ready printed tasting menu, one dish per page, built from our menu copy and our InDesign menu template with each graded dish photo dropped in, exported as a single print PDF; (3) an authored monochrome cover treatment of the dining-room ambience shot for the menu cover and the site header; (4) a matched web hero set of the catering spread for the site landing. Brand direction: warm, rich, premium, appetizing; consistent across every image; natural, not garish.

inputs.name: capture_01.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid shoot-day snapshot of a rustic bowl of Polish dumplings topped with browned butter onions and fresh dill on a dark ceramic plate, on a wooden restaurant table. Lit by warm tungsten pendant lights so the whole frame carries a distinct WARM/amber cast; slightly tilted horizon (~3 degrees); busy cluttered background of cutlery, a water glass and a folded napkin behind the plate. A small photographic 18% neutral grey reference card (a light/mid/dark three-patch card, no tint on the card itself) is clipped flat on the table in the lower-left corner, clearly visible. Real steam, dough texture, no studio gloss, documentary feel, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Signature hero and one of the CLUTTERED-background plates: the correct route is neutralize (this frame is warm, so COOL the temperature to its card), enrich the food warmth inside a semantic food selection, and lift the busy background out of focus with a subject-aware DoF blur so the dumplings read as hero. Its card is warm-skewed so the neutralization is real work. Tilted, so it must be straightened first. Naming is neutral so the agent must open it to decide hero-vs-flatlay and cluttered-vs-clean; nothing about the treatment sits in the filename.

inputs.name: capture_02.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal candid snapshot of a golden breaded schnitzel platter with a lemon wedge and parsley potatoes on a white plate, on a canteen table shot against a large cool north-facing window so the frame reads clearly COOL/blue and a touch under-exposed; cluttered background of napkins, a menu card and a second place setting. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card is propped flat at the frame edge, clearly visible. Real crumb texture, grease sheen, no CGI gloss, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Signature hero, cluttered background, and the OPPOSITE cast to capture_01 — cool/blue, so it must be WARMED to its card, proving a single shared white balance cannot serve both. Route: neutralize (warm), food-enrich, subject-aware background blur. Its card reads bluish. Same neutral naming; the cool-vs-warm split is only in these notes and the step notes.

inputs.name: capture_03.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal snapshot of a beet-and-goat-cheese salad with walnuts and greens on a slate board, lit by old overhead GREEN kitchen-pass fluorescent tubes so the whole frame carries a distinct sickly GREEN cast; cluttered table edge with a fork, crumbs and a bread basket behind. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card lies flat in a corner, visibly skewing green. Real produce texture, no studio polish, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Signature hero, cluttered background, and the TINT-axis case: its cast is green, NOT warm or cool, so a temperature move will never clear it — the correct neutralization pushes TINT toward magenta (with only a small temperature trim). This is the frame that most cleanly exposes a one-global-WB / temperature-only / auto-tone approach, because those cannot touch a green cast at all. Route: neutralize (magenta tint), food-enrich (keep the greens true, do not oversaturate), subject-aware background blur. Neutral naming.

inputs.name: capture_04.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal snapshot of a slice of layered Polish cheesecake with a deep amber-brown baked top and a berry coulis on a small plate, shot under clean near-neutral daylight on a tidy uncluttered marble counter with a clean soft-focus background already; the dessert is genuinely deep golden/amber in color. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card lies flat in a corner and already reads essentially neutral. Real crumb and cream texture, fork mark, no gloss, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRAP FRAME. This dish is genuinely deep-golden and it was shot under clean neutral light, so its in-frame grey card ALREADY reads neutral — the correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift, only matching exposure/brightness to the set. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool' or 'cool the warm' logic from the other frames, or 'cools an imagined amber cast', will neutralize this card OFF-neutral and strip the real color of the food. Decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch. It is also already shot CLEAN with a soft background, so it must NOT get a background blur — a hero plate that does not need isolating. Neutral naming so the agent cannot tell it apart from the cluttered heroes without opening it.

inputs.name: capture_05.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal snapshot of a tall glass of ruby-red Polish fruit compote drink with condensation and fruit pieces on a bar counter, lit by a single warm AMBER bar lamp so the frame is strongly warm; busy cluttered background of a shelf of bottles and glassware directly behind the glass. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card is clipped flat on the counter in view, skewing amber. Real glass reflections and droplets, no CGI, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Beverage hero, cluttered background, strong amber cast — a large COOL correction to its card, distinct in magnitude from capture_01's milder warm. Route: neutralize (cool), subject-aware background blur so the busy bottle shelf drops away and the glass reads as hero. No masked food-enrich needed (it is a drink, not a plated food with garnish hues to protect). Neutral naming.

inputs.name: capture_06.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal snapshot of a bowl of Polish sour rye soup with sliced sausage and egg in a bread bowl, on a plain wooden table with a clean uncluttered background, but the whole frame is clearly UNDEREXPOSED, muddy and flat with a faint cool cast. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card lies flat in a corner, sitting dark. Real steam and broth surface, no CGI, ~4000x3000px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Hero plate whose dominant problem is TONAL, not white balance: a large exposure + shadow lift plus contrast/clarity to defeat the muddiness, held so the recovered frame does not blow the highlights, then a small warm nudge to neutralize its faint-cool card to the shared white point — a single reasoned exposure-rescue whose magnitude is unique to this frame, so copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots. Its background is already clean, so it must NOT get a background blur. Neutral naming.

inputs.name: capture_07.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal OVERHEAD flat-lay of a catering grazing spread — cured meats, cheeses, olives, grapes, bread and dips arranged edge-to-edge across a large board and the surrounding table — shot under mixed cool canteen light so the frame reads slightly cool and flat; the horizon/board edge is tilted ~4 degrees. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card lies flat in one corner of the board, clearly visible. Real food texture, documentary shoot-day feel, no studio styling, ~4200x3200px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE FOIL #1: this is an overhead flat-lay where the ENTIRE surface is the subject — there is no single hero plate to isolate, so a subject-aware depth-of-field blur must NOT be applied (it would soften the outer dishes and destroy the whole composition). The correct route is straighten (tilted ~4 deg), neutralize its card to the shared white point, hold the house look, and crop the whole composition — never blur. It is the catering-spread web hero. Same neutral naming as the plated heroes, so the agent must open it and recognize it is a flat-lay, not a plate; the 'do not blur this' answer lives only here and in the step notes.

inputs.name: capture_08.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal OVERHEAD flat-lay of a dessert-and-coffee catering board — small pastries, a coffee pot, cups, and berries arranged across a linen-covered table — shot under warm window light so the frame reads warm; level. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card lies flat in one corner, skewing warm. Real texture, documentary feel, no studio styling, ~4200x3200px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: TRIAGE FOIL #2: a second overhead flat-lay — again the whole plane is the subject, so NO background blur (same trap as capture_07). Warm cast, so it must be cooled to its card (opposite direction to capture_07's cool cast), holding the house look. Delivered as a square social crop of the whole composition. Neutral naming.

inputs.name: capture_09.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal wide snapshot of a cozy modern Polish restaurant dining room with wooden tables, warm pendant lights and a bar, empty of people, shot handheld with a slightly tilted horizon (~2 degrees) and a flat, slightly cool exposure. A small photographic 18% neutral grey three-patch reference card is propped flat on the nearest table, clearly visible. Real ambient interior, documentary feel, no HDR, ~4200x3200px straight-off-camera.
inputs.realism_notes: Ambience shot and the base for the authored monochrome cover treatment. Route: straighten (tilted ~2 deg), neutralize its card to the shared white point and hold the house look like the rest, THEN author a distinctive whole-image monochrome/duotone treatment (image_apply_monochromatic_tint) for the menu cover and site header — an agent-authored designed look built from primitives, not a preset. Neutral naming.

inputs.name: kantyna_nova_house_look_note.pdf
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED one-page house-look note (supplied by the client, NOT model-generated and NOT a loadable develop preset): states the Kantyna Nova acceptance target in words and reference swatches only — on every graded frame the in-frame three-patch grey card must read neutral (equal across channels, no residual warm/blue/green tint) and its mid patch must sit at a consistent mid brightness across the set; the highlights must stay below clipping (no blown plates or paper); the darkest patch must stay off pure black; overall a warm premium restaurant tone with lifted shadows, a gentle contrast curve, enough clarity to resolve crumb/glaze/steam texture, and a restrained vibrance lift so the food is appetizing without oversaturating. It is a target to build by eye and hold identical across the batch, not a preset to apply.
inputs.realism_notes: Deliberately a written/visual TARGET, not an .xmp or a built-in preset name — this is the fix for the audited G6 defect (the prior task hand-graded one hero then applied a STOCK preset to the siblings, which cannot reproduce a hand-built grade, so nothing could actually match). The agent must BUILD the look from primitive tone controls (image_apply_adjustments) and hold it identical, neutralizing each frame to its in-frame card BY EYE — there is no preset to lean on. The numeric card tolerances belong to the grader, never to a step the agent performs; the agent never reads a pixel.

inputs.name: kantyna_nova_menu_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A5 portrait tasting-menu page — ONE dish per page. It carries live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<dish_name>>, <<dish_desc>> and <<price>>, plus ONE @-prefixed image-path merge column bound to a full-bleed dish-photo frame at the top of the page: @image resolves to that row's graded dish photo. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and the image field actually bind; A5 (148x210mm) portrait with 3mm bleed, set up for ~300 DPI print. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-up grid would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus a genuine @image-path column, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a one-dish-per-page tasting menu is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. The @image column binds the AGENT's own graded/cropped dish crops (the agent names each per its content-match of capture to dish), so the routing answer never sits in a field the agent is handed.

inputs.name: kantyna_nova_menu_copy.tsv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a TSV with columns dish_name<TAB>dish_desc<TAB>price<TAB>@image holding 6 tasting-menu rows, one per plated dish: a dumpling bowl with browned onions, a breaded schnitzel platter, a beet-and-goat-cheese salad, a layered baked cheesecake slice, a ruby fruit-compote drink, and a sour rye soup in a bread bowl. Each row carries a short evocative one-to-two-line menu description and a price in the local format (e.g. 32 zl). The @image column names the matching prepped dish crop the editor will produce (the editor fills it after matching each menu row to the correct capture and grading/cropping it), so the [T] merge drops each graded dish photo into that row's single-record page. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<dish_name>>,<<dish_desc>>,<<price>> and the @image column.
inputs.realism_notes: Honors the brief's menu copy; headers match the authored .indd fields and the @image column so the one-file-per-row [T] merge binds copy and the correct photo per dish. Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six pages. The rows describe dishes by CONTENT (the menu copy), which the agent content-matches to the right capture; nothing in the copy telegraphs the per-frame grade treatment or which captures are flat-lays. The @image cells reference the agent's own output crop names, filled per its triage — the answer is not handed to it.

outputs.name: graded_masters_contact_set_x9
outputs.spec: The nine grey-card-neutralized, straightened masters as one matched contact set, RETAINED with the in-frame grey card still present (these are the neutrality-grading artifacts). Each frame corrected on its OWN terms to its card — the warm frames cooled, the cool frame warmed, the green frame pushed on the tint axis toward magenta, the already-neutral golden dish held, the underexposed frame exposure-rescued, the two flat-lays neutralized on opposite casts — then the single authored house look (warm premium tone, lifted shadows, gentle contrast, clarity, restrained vibrance, built from primitive adjustments, no preset) held identical across all nine; full-res (~4000-4200px long edge). Acceptance (grader-checked, on THESE retained card-bearing masters, never on a card-cropped deliverable): every frame's three grey patches read neutral within a tight channel-spread tolerance, the mid patch matches a shared mid-grey level across the set, the highlights stay below the clip ceiling and the darkest patch stays off pure black; and the golden trap frame's card is neutral WITHOUT its real food color having been cooled off. The grader measures these on the output; the agent does not.

outputs.name: Kantyna_Nova_tasting_menu.pdf
outputs.spec: The agent-owned designed endpoint: a press-ready A5 (148x210mm) portrait tasting menu, ONE dish per page (page-count = menu-copy row-count = 6), exported from the one-file-per-row InDesign data-merge. Each page binds its dish_name/dish_desc/price verbatim from the menu copy with its matching graded, background-treated dish photo dropped into the full-bleed image frame via @image (a merge bind, never free-form placement); ~300 DPI at trim with 3mm bleed. The dish crops are framed on the food with the grey card cropped OUT — card-exclusion is checked here, separately, and the card's neutrality is graded only on the retained contact-set masters, never on these crops. The cluttered hero plates arrive here with their busy backgrounds thrown out of focus so the dish reads as hero; the already-clean plates arrive sharp and untouched — the routing decision is visible on the printed page.

outputs.name: kantyna_nova_ambience_cover_mono
outputs.spec: An authored monochrome/duotone treatment of the graded dining-room ambience shot (capture_09) for the menu cover and the site header — a whole-image monochromatic tone the agent builds from primitives (image_apply_monochromatic_tint on the neutralized, straightened master), giving the cover a distinctive, deliberately-designed mood rather than a canned filter. Delivered cropped to a wide header frame, sRGB, web-light.

outputs.name: catering_spread_web_hero_set
outputs.spec: A matched web hero set of the catering grazing flat-lay (capture_07) cut from its graded master for the site landing: a desktop crop (1920px wide, 16:9) and a mobile crop (1080px wide, 4:5) of the WHOLE overhead composition, subject-centered, sRGB, web-light. Delivered sharp — this flat-lay is never background-blurred, since the whole spread is the subject.

outputs.name: grade_parameter_report
outputs.spec: A short accompanying note (secondary to the images, NOT the primary deliverable) in which the agent reports, per capture (capture_01..capture_09), the final correction it APPLIED — the temperature and tint direction and amount, the exposure/highlight/shadow move, and the contrast/clarity/vibrance of the shared house look — and names which axis carried each frame (cool-to-neutral, warm-to-neutral, magenta tint for the green frame, exposure-rescue for the muddy frame, WB HELD for the already-neutral golden frame) plus which shots it routed to a background blur and which it deliberately left alone. This is an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement: the agent knows these values because it set them by eye. It makes the divergent per-frame reasoning and the blur routing visible and exposes whether one recipe was lazily copied across opposite casts. Acceptance (grader-checked): the nine reported corrections are non-identical and their directions match each frame's cast (in particular a tint move on the green frame, opposite temperature moves on the warm vs cool frames, and WB held on the golden frame), and the blur routing matches the hero/flat-lay/clean split.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: capture_01.jpg, capture_02.jpg, capture_03.jpg, capture_04.jpg, capture_05.jpg, capture_06.jpg, capture_07.jpg, capture_08.jpg, capture_09.jpg, kantyna_nova_house_look_note.pdf, kantyna_nova_menu_template.indd, kantyna_nova_menu_copy.tsv
connector_workflow.note: Ingest the nine raw captures plus the house-look note, the authored menu template and the menu copy so every downstream edit runs against real asset references. Plumbing, not difficulty.
capture_01 is tilted ~3 deg — level it first (auto_straighten is the ONLY tool that rectifies a tilt). Only the tilted frames (01, 07, 09) get this; deciding which are tilted is part of the job.

capture_01 is warm tungsten: judge the amber cast by eye off its grey card and COOL the temperature (dial and record the temp; add a small tint only if the card also skews green) until the three patches read neutral and the mid patch sits at the shared mid-grey, lifting exposure/shadows out of the flat baseline. Then lay in the authored house look built here from primitives — a gentle contrast curve, clarity to resolve the crumb and steam, highlights held below clipping, blacks just off pure black, a restrained vibrance lift. Single authored adjustments call, NOT a preset and NOT auto-tone. Report the move.

Semantic selection of only the plated food ('the bowl of dumplings with onions and dill on the plate'), so the food warmth can be enriched without dragging the plate, table or grey card. Semantic object selection — never a hue or coordinate selection. Returns a maskURI.

Masked food-enrich (consumes the neutralized frame AND the food mask): within the selection only, a small in-band warm-hue nudge plus a modest saturation/luminance lift so the browned onions and dough read rich and appetizing while the plate whites and the grey card stay neutral. Bounded, in-band — well under the tool's ~90 deg ceiling, no near-complementary rotation. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolor path; image_apply_color_overlay is whole-image (would tint the plate and card) and image_fill_area is a flat dead-fill (would kill the food texture), so both are wrong here. This masked pass is part of the agent-authored look.

ROUTING DECISION: capture_01 is a single plated hero on a CLUTTERED table, so throw the busy cutlery/glass background out of focus with a subject-aware depth-of-field blur that keeps the plate sharp and softens the clutter behind it, so the dish reads as hero. This is applied ONLY to the cluttered hero plates (01, 02, 03, 05); the already-clean plates (04, 06) and the overhead flat-lays (07, 08) are deliberately NOT blurred — see their steps.

Crop the finished hero to the full-bleed A5 dish frame the menu template expects, framing on the food with the grey card cropped OUT — this card-excluded crop is what binds into that dish's menu page via @image. The card's neutrality is graded on the retained c01_neutral master, never on this crop. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only from the ~4000px source, never generative-expand/upscale.

capture_02 is cool north-window and slightly under: the OPPOSITE move to capture_01 — WARM the temperature toward the same neutral card target and lift exposure, then apply the identical house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance character so it matches the set. Applying capture_01's cooling here would push this frame further blue — judging the card by eye is what tells the agent to reverse direction. Report the warming amount dialed.
Semantic selection of only the plated food ('the breaded schnitzel platter with lemon and potatoes on the plate') for a skin-safe-equivalent food enrich. Returns a maskURI.

Masked food-enrich within the food selection only: warm the golden crumb and settle the potatoes without dragging the white plate or the grey card. Bounded in-band shift, same authored-look move as capture_01.
ROUTING DECISION: capture_02 is a cluttered hero plate (napkins, menu card, second setting behind it), so apply the subject-aware background DoF blur to lift the platter off the clutter.
Crop to the full-bleed A5 dish frame, food-framed, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

capture_03 is the GREEN fluorescent frame — the TINT-axis case. It does NOT move on the warm/cool axis: judge the green card by eye and push TINT toward MAGENTA to neutralize it (with only a small temperature trim), then seat the mid/highlights/blacks on the shared target and apply the identical house look. A temperature-only correction, one global WB copied from the warm or cool frames, or an auto-tone pass cannot clear a green cast at all — this frame's card would stay green while the others look fixed, the visible failure this gate catches. Report the magenta tint amount and confirm it is a tint (not a temperature) move.

Semantic selection of only the salad ('the beet and goat-cheese salad with walnuts and greens on the slate board') so the food can be enriched without oversaturating the greens or touching the grey card. Returns a maskURI.

Masked food-enrich within the salad only: deepen the beet reds and keep the greens true and natural (a restrained saturation lift, NOT a push that goes garish), luminance held so texture survives. Bounded in-band. Part of the authored look.
ROUTING DECISION: capture_03 is a cluttered hero (fork, crumbs, bread basket behind), so apply the subject-aware background DoF blur to lift the salad off the clutter.
Crop to the full-bleed A5 dish frame, food-framed, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

capture_04 is THE TRAP: the cheesecake is genuinely deep-golden and it was shot under clean neutral light, so its grey card ALREADY reads neutral. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift — only match exposure/brightness to the set mid-grey and apply the same house-look contrast/clarity/vibrance. A naive agent that batch-applies the 'warm the cool / cool the warm' logic from the other frames, or 'cools an imagined amber cast', will neutralize this card OFF-neutral and strip the real color of the food. Drive the decision off THIS card, not the batch. Report that WB was HELD.

ROUTING DECISION: capture_04 was shot CLEAN with a soft background, so it needs NO background blur — a hero plate that does not need isolating. Crop straight to the full-bleed A5 dish frame, food-framed, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Blurring an already-clean plate would be the wrong route.
capture_05 is strongly warm amber (bar lamp): a large COOL correction to its card, distinct in magnitude from capture_01's milder warm, then the shared house look. Report the (larger) cooling move.

ROUTING DECISION: capture_05 is a cluttered beverage hero (busy bottle shelf directly behind the glass), so apply the subject-aware background DoF blur so the shelf drops away and the glass reads as hero. No masked food-enrich here — it is a drink, not a plated food with garnish hues to protect.
Crop to the full-bleed A5 dish frame, subject-framed on the glass, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

capture_06 is muddy and UNDEREXPOSED with a faint cool cast: the dominant move is TONAL — a large exposure + shadow lift plus contrast/clarity to defeat the muddiness, held so the recovered frame keeps the highlights below clipping and the dark card patch off pure black — plus a small warm nudge to neutralize its faint-cool card to the shared white point. The magnitude of this lift is unique to this frame; copying any other frame's exposure here visibly under- or over-shoots. Report the exposure/shadow/contrast moves dialed.

ROUTING DECISION: capture_06's background is already clean, so NO background blur. Crop straight to the full-bleed A5 dish frame, food-framed, grey card cropped OUT. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only.

Nine per-frame grade sub-chains fan out from batch_uploaded, each a DIFFERENT authored correction driven to that frame's own in-frame grey card, not a repeated call: capture_01 warm->cool (straighten first), capture_02 cool->warm (opposite direction), capture_03 green->magenta on the TINT axis, capture_04 WB HELD (already-neutral golden trap), capture_05 strong amber->cool of unique magnitude, capture_06 exposure-rescue of unique magnitude, capture_07 cool->warm flat-lay (straighten first), capture_08 warm->cool flat-lay, capture_09 cool->warm ambience (straighten first). The single authored house look (built from image_apply_adjustments primitives) is held identical across all nine; there is no preset and no auto-tone. The three cluttered signature plates (01/02/03) additionally run image_select_by_prompt->masked image_adjust_hsl food-enrich; the four cluttered hero plates (01/02/03/05) route through image_apply_lens_blur while the clean plates (04/06) and the two flat-lays (07/08) deliberately do NOT — the blur routing is a per-frame decision. Six dish crops (grey card cropped OUT) feed the menu; the flat-lays feed the web hero set (07 -> desktop+mobile) and a social square (08); the ambience master runs image_apply_monochromatic_tint(33)->crop(34) into the authored cover. The six dish crops converge into the upload session(35)->finalize(36)->document_merge_data_layout(37), which also consumes the authored .indd and the menu copy and emits one merged page per row, then document_render_layout(38) exports the whole six-page menu once. The nine retained *_neutral masters (grey card in frame) are the neutrality-grading contact set; nothing after the single ingest originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 38 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* grading/masking/blur/tint/crop, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single ingest and the two upload steps. The core is not a repeated recipe: each of the nine neutralizations is a DIFFERENT reasoned decision (warm frames cooled, cool frames warmed, the green frame pushed on the tint axis, the genuinely-golden frame HELD, the muddy frame exposure-rescued, two flat-lays neutralized on opposite casts) all forced to converge on one measurable target — the in-frame 18% grey card — so a blanket correction, a copied recipe, or per-frame auto-tone cannot pass. This directly fixes the audited G6 defect: the prior task hand-graded one hero then applied a STOCK built-in preset to seven siblings (which cannot reproduce a hand-built grade, so the set could never match); here the house look is AUTHORED from primitives and held identical, and cohesion is checkable against the cards. Layered on top: a masked luminosity-preserving food-enrich on the signature plates (a bounded in-band shift image_adjust_hsl can hold), a three-way per-shot background-separation triage (cluttered hero plates get a subject-aware DoF blur, clean plates and overhead flat-lays do NOT), an authored monochrome cover treatment from primitives, and a one-record-per-page data-merge into a hand-authored A5 menu template ending in a single press-ready export. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (camera-scale ~4000-4200px sources, all crops downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'), no inpainting/object-removal (the 'make the food read' ask is honored by grade + subject-aware DoF blur, never reconstruction), convert_pdf_to_indd NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd), image_fill_area unused, image_apply_color_overlay unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _dark_portions / _vibrance_and_saturation / _brightness_and_contrast / _exposure are replaced by image_apply_adjustments, and image_list_presets / image_apply_preset are removed entirely.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a craft decision with a visible failure mode, never a self-measurement): (1) every capture carries an in-frame 18% grey card and the acceptance test is that each card, graded on its RETAINED pre-crop *_neutral master (card still in frame), reads a clean neutral with the whole set on one shared white point — a naive agent that copies one white-balance across the batch, applies one stock preset for 'cohesion', or auto-tones each frame leaves the cool frame blue, the warm frames amber and the green frame green and fails the gate, since the six start on divergent casts across two colour axes and a move that rescues one drives another off; the required grade_parameter_report (an APPLIED-settings log, not a measurement) exposes copied-recipe laziness directly. (2) A three-way per-shot background-separation triage: the cluttered hero plates need a subject-aware DoF blur to lift the dish off the clutter, but the already-clean plates need nothing and the two OVERHEAD FLAT-LAYS must never be blurred (a DoF blur softens the outer dishes and wrecks the whole spread) — the captures share a neutral naming scheme so the agent must open each and decide, and a wrong route is invisible until it prints. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (a) cross-asset neutralization of nine differently-lit shots to a common measurable card target on differing correction axes (warm/cool temperature, green/magenta tint, exposure-rescue), which a novice cannot match by eye; (b) the flat-lay-vs-hero blur triage plus the masked food-enrich constraint (enrich the food warmth without dragging the plate whites, the garnish greens or the grey card — only a semantic select isolates it, not a hue selection). TRAP: the genuinely-golden cheesecake (capture_04) was shot under clean light so its card is already neutral — batch-applying the other frames' 'correct the cast' logic, or cooling an imagined amber cast, pushes its card off-neutral and strips the real food color; the correct path reads THAT card and HOLDS white balance. A second trap: reaching for one global WB / one stock preset / per-frame auto-tone for 'cohesion' visibly fails at the cards (the exact defect the audit flagged), and blurring a flat-lay wrecks it. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) every grey card reads true-neutral within a channel-spread tolerance with the mid patch on a shared mid-grey, highlights below clipping and blacks off pure black, evaluated on the nine RETAINED card-bearing *_neutral masters (never on a card-removed crop), including the golden trap frame neutral WITHOUT its food color cooled off; (b) card-exclusion checked separately on the dish/flat-lay crops that ship; (c) the grade_parameter_report lists non-identical per-frame corrections whose directions match each frame's cast and a blur routing that matches the hero/clean/flat-lay split; (d) the tasting menu is exactly six pages (page-count = menu-copy row-count) at ~300 DPI A5 with bleed — so 'matched, routed and composed' is checkable rather than asserted, and the agent supplies parameters it applied rather than values it read.
